40d9765070.what_happened: At least 10 people were killed and 13 injured when protesters and security forces clashed in Balato, Siguiri region, over enforcement of a gold mining ban. Two pick‑up trucks and a security forces truck were burned, and a firearm and motorcycle were seized by protesters. Five foreign nationals were among the dead, and the cause of the violence is still under investigation.
details: The Ministry of Territorial Administration said late on Thursday that clashes occurred on Wednesday when security forces were verifying the implementation of the artisanal gold mining ban. Protesters erected barricades blocking the patrol, leading to exchanges of gunfire, though it was unclear who opened fire. The injured included civilians and members of the security forces.

Guinea banned artisanal gold mining in Siguiri on November 2 because miners failed to comply with regulations, causing environmental damage such as farmland destruction and river pollution. The government said the restrictions aim to curb this damage, and judicial authorities are tasked with determining what triggered the violence and who is responsible. Over 1,200 people were arrested earlier this month, and the first mass trials have opened this week.

Neighbouring Mali reported that about 100,000 people arrived in Bamako and nearly 60,000 more in Kouremale after being forced out of Guinea when the mining ban was announced. Burkina Faso said it repatriated 45,406 of its citizens who left Guinea because of the ban. Artisanal gold mining supports more than 300,000 livelihoods in Guinea, according to the UN Environment Programme, and is driven by rising metal demand across West Africa.
key_facts: At least 10 killed and 13 injured in Balato, Siguiri region clashes.
Protesters and security forces clashed over enforcement of artisanal gold mining ban.

a827be0853.what_happened: Sri Lanka joined 150 other countries in supporting a United Nations resolution on Palestinian sovereignty over natural resources in occupied territories, including East Jerusalem. The UN General Assembly’s Second Committee approved it on November 11, 2026, with 151 votes in favour, seven against and 11 abstaining. The United States, Israel, Colombia, Micronesia, Nauru, Palau and Paraguay voted against it.
details: According to Newswire, Sri Lanka joined 150 other countries in supporting a United Nations resolution that affirms the permanent sovereignty of the Palestinian people over their natural resources in the occupied Palestinian territories, including East Jerusalem. The United Nations General Assembly’s Second Committee approved the resolution on November 11, 2026. The vote was 151 countries in favour, seven against, and 11 abstaining.

The seven countries that voted against were the United States, Israel, Colombia, Micronesia, Nauru, Palau and Paraguay. Sri Lanka voted in favour alongside countries including India, China and the United Kingdom. The resolution is titled Permanent sovereignty of the Palestinian people in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and of the Arab population in the occupied Syrian Golan over their natural resources.

It reaffirms that people living under occupation have the right to control and benefit from their natural resources. It addresses concerns over the exploitation, damage and depletion of natural resources, including land and water resources, in the occupied territories. The text calls on Israel, as the occupying power, to stop activities that exploit or destroy Palestinian natural resources, and recognises the Palestinians’ right to seek compensation for losses caused by such activities.

The vote shows broad international support for Palestinian economic rights and sovereignty amid continuing concerns over conditions in the occupied territories. Sri Lanka has maintained longstanding support for Palestinian self-determination and a negotiated two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The resolution was approved at the committee stage and will proceed to the full UN General Assembly for final consideration, though it is not legally binding and carries political significance as an expression of UN member states’ positions.
a827be0853.why_it_matters: The vote reflects broad international support for Palestinian economic rights and sovereignty, and the resolution carries political significance as an expression of UN member states’ positions.

a827be0853.whats_next: It will proceed to the full UN General Assembly for final consideration.
a827be0853.blurb: Sri Lanka backed a UN resolution on Palestinian natural resources as 151 nations voted in favour.

039e29e21e.what_happened: Maryland senator Chris Van Hollen announced he will challenge Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer for the party’s top leadership post. The contest, which will decide the Democratic Party’s direction as it prepares to control the Senate next year, will be decided at a closed‑door caucus meeting on 1 December. Schumer says he has the votes, while Van Hollen is considered an underdog and has secured progressive endorsements.
details: Chris Van Hollen, a 67‑year‑old Maryland senator, declared his candidacy to replace Chuck Schumer, who is 75 and has led Senate Democrats since 2017. Schumer expressed confidence he retains the votes needed, while Van Hollen called himself an underdog.

The race will be settled at a private Senate Democratic caucus meeting scheduled for 1 December, after the party’s midterm victories gave it its largest Senate and House majorities in years. Progressive groups have praised Van Hollen’s bid, and he has gathered several endorsements, whereas Schumer has support from senators across the ideological spectrum.

The Senate’s 60‑vote filibuster makes the leader pivotal in confronting the Republican‑led majority, especially as Trump returns to the White House in 2025. Schumer previously backed a GOP‑supported spending bill in March 2025, drawing anger from House Democrats and activist groups, while Van Hollen has criticized Israel and voted against providing weapons to the country.
039e29e21e.why_it_matters: It will determine the Democratic Party’s strategy and leadership as it prepares to control the Senate next year.

039e29e21e.blurb: Maryland’s Chris Van Hollen challenges longtime leader Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic chief as the party prepares to wield power next year.

713ea05b6a.what_happened: A tanker called Atlantic Asphalt hit the docked river cruise ship American Heritage on the Mississippi River in New Orleans at about 12.30pm on Friday. Rescue crews pulled people from the water as the cruise ship slowly rolled onto its side, and 24 patients were admitted to hospital. The river was closed to all vessel traffic while responders worked.
details: The tanker Atlantic Asphalt collided with American Cruise Lines' American Heritage at about 12.30pm on Friday while it was docked on the Mississippi River in New Orleans, said Kimberly Curth, Port of New Orleans press secretary. The cruise ship had about 129 passengers plus crew onboard and had docked about two hours earlier to begin passenger disembarkation.

New Orleans firefighters, port and city police, the US Coast Guard and emergency medical staff worked to pull people from the water, and mayor Helena Moreno's office said multiple individuals had been rescued. Video showed tugboat crew pulling people in lifejackets or holding flotation rings from the river, and those who got off were brought inside the port's administration building. LCMC, which runs University Medical Center, said 24 patients were admitted, Acadian Ambulance took eight people to hospital with injuries not yet known, and the Coast Guard closed the river to all vessel traffic between mile markers 93 and 96.

Video showed the American Heritage slowly roll onto its side, and witness Jamie Holford told WDSU it took 15 minutes from impact to rolling over, calling it surreal. Maritime law expert Martin J Davies of Tulane University told WVUE the tanker was lucky not to strike the Crescent City Connection bridge, which carries about 160,000 cars daily. Officials gave no cause; one emergency source said the tanker may have lost power, unconfirmed, and American Cruise Lines said guests and crew were evacuated without giving numbers.

The American Heritage is a 300ft paddle-wheel ship built in 2015, previously the Queen of the Mississippi, with more than 80 staterooms; the Atlantic Asphalt is an oil tanker built in 2017, about 160 meters long, deadweight 17,764 metric tons, flying the Marshall Islands flag, owned and commercially operated by Nave Shipping SA, a company registered in Liberia, with maintenance, technical and safety work overseen by Singapore-based Thome Ship Management. It is not on international sanctions lists checked by services including Magic Port, but Canadian authorities fined it C$7,800, recorded 11 August 2020, after an officer failed to properly supervise a transfer operation. Rescue activity scaled back later on Friday, and Louisiana governor Jeff Landry said he was headed to New Orleans.
713ea05b6a.whats_next: The river stays closed to all vessel traffic between mile markers 93 and 96 while responders assess the situation, and Louisiana governor Jeff Landry said he was headed to New Orleans.

de245bbe1f.what_happened: An asphalt tanker collided with a river cruise boat on the Mississippi River in New Orleans, causing the boat to partially submerge and flip. Dozens of passengers were hospitalized, but all were accounted for with no critical injuries. Rescue operations involving multiple agencies are ongoing.
details: The Atlantic Asphalt tanker struck the American Heritage paddleboat on Friday at about 12:30pm local time (18:30 GMT) in New Orleans. The cruise boat had docked two hours earlier to disembark passengers when the collision occurred, causing it to sink and topple over. Mayor Helena Moreno stated that all 129 passengers were accounted for, with 32 taken to local hospitals, none with critical injuries.

Passengers were seen entering the water as the boat listed, with water temperature at 19 degrees Celsius (66 degrees Fahrenheit). More than a dozen people in life jackets were rescued from the river onto nearby ships. Witness Jamie Holford described the event as 'surreal,' noting it took 15 minutes from impact to the boat rolling over.

Port police, the fire department, the coastguard, and emergency medical staff responded to the scene, setting up a triage area in the port's administration building. The river was closed to vessel traffic. American Cruise Lines, which operates the boat, confirmed the evacuation of guests and crew, expressing concern for those involved. The American Heritage, built in 2015, holds up to 150 passengers and was on an eight-day cruise. The 160-metre tanker, flagged in the Marshall Islands, specializes in asphalt and bitumen, but the cause of the collision and whether it carried cargo remains unknown.
key_facts: Tanker hit cruise boat in New Orleans on Friday at 12:30pm.
129 passengers on board, all accounted for, 32 hospitalized with no critical injuries.
Water temperature was 19°C (66°F), rescue teams pulled people from river.
American Heritage boat was built in 2015, holds up to 150 passengers.
Tanker was 160 metres long, flagged in Marshall Islands, bound for New Orleans.
Cause of collision and cargo status unknown, river closed to traffic.
de245bbe1f.blurb: A tanker collision in New Orleans sinks a cruise boat, sparking a major rescue operation with 32 hospitalized but no critical injuries.

d368103041.what_happened: The United States has lost its measles-free status, 26 years after the disease was declared eliminated there, as the country battles its highest measles case count in more than 30 years. Pennsylvania and Wisconsin each announced one additional measles-associated death on Friday, bringing the total to 10 deaths this year. Federal and state officials are now disputing how measles deaths should be counted.
details: The United States has lost its measles-free status, 26 years after measles was declared eliminated there in 2000, US media reported. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) revoked the status, first reported by The Wall Street Journal, after determining uninterrupted measles transmission for more than 12 months. More than 5,400 confirmed cases have been recorded to date, per CDC and Johns Hopkins University International Vaccine Access Center tracker data, with cases as of November 2026 more than double the 2,289 confirmed in 2025.

Pennsylvania and Wisconsin each announced one additional measles-associated death on Friday, marking 10 total US deaths linked to the disease this year. Wisconsin's Department of Health Services reported an infant's death, while Pennsylvania's Department of Health said its latest death was an unvaccinated patient who tested positive for measles. Pennsylvania has logged seven measles-associated deaths and Wisconsin two, and on November 2 New York said a child died in the state's first recorded measles death in more than 30 years.

Al Jazeera reports about 7,500 people infected and 13 deaths since last year, a period coinciding with the tenure of Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, who has for years spread doubts without scientific evidence about measles vaccine safety. The CDC recorded six measles-related deaths, twice its 2025 figure, but its national toll is lower than state-reported numbers after Kennedy asked CDC director Erica Schwartz not to count the deaths, claiming no evidence they were measles-associated. The count is at the centre of a dispute between Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro and Kennedy; Pennsylvania counts a death as measles-associated when a confirmed case dies within 30 days of symptoms, unless it resulted from an unrelated event.

The CDC says it is working with the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists on a standardised definition for measles deaths, but infectious disease experts warn the dispute puts the agency at odds with longstanding tracking practice used by the WHO and CDC. Vaccination coverage among US kindergarteners fell from 95.2 percent in the 2019-2020 school year to 92.4 percent in 2025-2026, and local and state health departments have ramped up vaccination efforts. Measles is preventable through the MMR vaccine, which offers about 97 percent protection after two doses; Canada, Spain and the United Kingdom recently lost elimination status after a WHO expert review, and the US left the WHO but remains a PAHO member.
d368103041.why_it_matters: Measles is highly contagious and preventable, and losing elimination status after 26 years follows the highest case numbers in more than 30 years amid falling kindergarten vaccination coverage.
